why: tenants ______ needs an object, and that object is concerns, earlier in the sentence. Only raised takes concerns directly.
tenants ______ 缺受詞，受詞是前面的 concerns。只有 raised 能直接接 concerns。
usage: speak about a topic, or speak at an event; it cannot take concerns directly. Two tenants spoke about the noise.
speak about 主題，或在場合中發言；不能直接接 concerns。
comment on something. Several tenants commented on the new parking rules.
comment on 某事。
complain about something, or complain that…; it needs about before the problem. Tenants complained about the noise.
complain about 某事，或接 that 子句；問題前面要有 about。

gloss.ex: Each tenant pays rent on the first day.
Please pass on my thanks to the team.
The property management company fixed the heating.

why: The subject of will be ______ is The vacancy at the start, not office. A vacancy is an empty job, so it gets filled by an internal candidate.
will be ______ 的主詞是句首的 The vacancy，不是 office。職缺是空的，要被補上：filled by an internal candidate。
usage: hold a post or a position: someone keeps a job that is already theirs. She holds the senior buyer position.
hold a post／position：擔任已經屬於自己的職位。
occupy a room, a building or a position; people take up a space. Three departments occupy the second floor.
occupy 房間、樓層或職位：占用空間。
assume a role or a responsibility: take it on. He assumed the role of team leader in May.
assume a role／responsibility：接下角色或責任。

gloss.ex: We have a vacancy in the sales team.
She transferred to the Boston office last year.
We interviewed one internal candidate for the job.

why: The fixed phrase is at short notice, meaning with very little time to prepare. At such short leads straight to notice.
固定說法是 at short notice，指事前幾乎沒時間準備。at such short 後面直接接 notice。
usage: warning is a signal of possible trouble: without warning, a warning sign. The storm came without warning.
warning 是可能有麻煩的預告：without warning、a warning sign。
time is used in on time, in time and at the same time. The bus arrived on time.
time 用在 on time、in time、at the same time。
alert is a signal or message about danger or news. The app sent an alert about the delay.
alert 是關於危險或消息的警示訊息。

gloss.ex: He resigned to start his own firm.
She works the night shift on Fridays.
We hired a temp agency for the summer.

why: The blank comes before unlikely. The adverb that strengthens likely or unlikely is highly: highly unlikely.
空格在 unlikely 前面。加強 likely／unlikely 的副詞是 highly：highly unlikely。
usage: strongly goes with verbs of opinion or feeling: recommend, believe, disagree. We strongly recommend booking early.
strongly 搭表示意見或感受的動詞：recommend、believe、disagree。
greatly adds force to a verb or a comparison: greatly improved, greatly reduced. Sales have greatly improved.
greatly 加強動詞或比較：greatly improved、greatly reduced。
heavily goes with rely, invest and depend. The firm relies heavily on one supplier.
heavily 搭 rely、invest、depend。

gloss.ex: The container ship reached the harbor on Monday.
Workers unload the truck every morning.
The congested road delayed our delivery.

why: All four mean roughly “not allow.” The difference is what follows the person. After whether permanent or temporary comes to keep, and only forbid takes someone + to do.
四個都是「禁止」，差在人後面接什麼。whether permanent or temporary 之後是 to keep，只有 forbid 接「人＋to V」。
usage: prohibit someone from doing something. The rules prohibit staff from eating at their desks.
prohibit 人 from Ving。
prevent someone from doing something; it means stopping it from happening, not a rule. The fence prevents visitors from entering the site.
prevent 人 from Ving；意思是阻止事情發生，不是規定。
ban something, or ban someone from doing something. The airline bans passengers from smoking on board.
ban 某事，或 ban 人 from Ving。

gloss.ex: The billing department sends invoices on Fridays.
She became a permanent employee in June.
We hired temporary staff for the sale.

point: substitute A for B：用 A 取代 B。
why: The new item comes first and the old one after for: a platter of fresh seasonal fruit for the almond cake. Only substituted fits that pattern.
新的在前、舊的在 for 後：a platter of fresh seasonal fruit for the almond cake。只有 substituted 符合這個句型。
usage: replace the old thing with the new one. The hotel replaced its old carpets with wooden floors.
replace 舊的 with 新的。
exchange A for B: give A and get B back, often in a shop. She exchanged the shirt for a larger size.
exchange A for B：交出 A、換回 B，常見於商店。
remove something from a place or a list; it does not say what takes its place. Staff removed the old sign from the door.
remove 某物 from 某處；沒有說換成什麼。

gloss.ex: He has an allergy to shellfish.
The caterer arrived two hours before the party.
She served a cheese platter at the reception.

point: 事物 cost 人 金額。
why: The subject of the blank is The repairs, not contractor. When something takes money from someone, the verb is cost: cost the company nearly $8,000.
空格的主詞是 The repairs，不是 contractor。某事讓某人花掉多少錢，動詞用 cost：cost the company nearly $8,000。
usage: charge someone an amount: the seller asks for the money. The plumber charged us $200 for the visit.
charge 人 金額：收錢的人開價。
spend money on something; the subject is the person paying. The firm spent $5,000 on new signs.
spend 錢 on 某事；主詞是花錢的人。
pay someone, or pay for something; the subject is the person giving money. The company paid the contractor last week.
pay 人，或 pay for 某物；主詞是付錢的人。

gloss.ex: We hired a roofing contractor for the repairs.
Staff carried out the survey in May.
The estimate was higher than we expected.

why: Take out within the first six months alone, and the blank is followed by in a sharp drop. Only resulted takes in: has resulted in a sharp drop.
拿掉 within the first six months alone，空格後面是 in a sharp drop。只有 resulted 接 in：has resulted in a sharp drop。
usage: lead to something; it takes to, not in. The delay led to several complaints.
lead to 某事；接 to，不接 in。
cause something directly, with no preposition. The storm caused a power cut.
cause 直接接受詞，不加介系詞。
produce something directly: make it or bring it about. The new process produced fewer errors.
produce 直接接受詞：製造或帶來某結果。

gloss.ex: Sales figures rose in the third quarter.
The bank opened a branch downtown.
There was a sharp drop in orders.

point: deductible: the amount you pay first on a claim.
deductible：理賠時自己先付的額度（自負額）。
why: The bill was $1,600 and the insurer paid only $600. The missing $1,000 is what the company pays itself before cover starts: the deductible.
帳單 1,600，保險公司只付了 600。差的 1,000 是公司在保險給付前自己先付的額度：deductible。
usage: premium is the regular payment for an insurance policy. The company pays its insurance premium every month.
premium 是為保單定期繳的保費。
surcharge is an extra fee added to a price. The airline added a fuel surcharge.
surcharge 是加在價格上的額外費用。
rebate is money paid back after you have paid. Buyers get a $50 rebate on this printer.
rebate 是付款後退回的錢。

gloss.ex: The insurer approved the claim in two days.
Our insurance policy covers water damage.
A minor accident delayed the delivery.

why: Whereas sets two groups against each other. Vendors who withdraw early get the full amount back, so those who withdraw late lose the deposit: forfeit.
whereas 把兩組人對比。早退出的人 get the full amount back，所以晚退出的人失去訂金：forfeit。
usage: reclaim something: collect or get back what is yours. Passengers reclaim their luggage after landing.
reclaim：取回屬於自己的東西。
refund money to someone; the one who received the payment gives it back. The shop refunded the customer in full.
refund：收款的一方把錢退還給對方。
redeem a voucher, coupon or points: exchange it for goods. She redeemed the coupon at the checkout.
redeem 禮券、優惠券或點數：兌換成商品。

gloss.ex: Several vendors sell fresh bread at the fair.
She had to withdraw from the contest.
Each vendor rents a stall at the market.

point: creditor: a person or firm the company owes.
creditor：債權人（公司欠錢的對象）。
why: Until the invoice has been paid in full, the company still owes the supplier money. A business that is owed money is a creditor.
發票 has been paid in full 之前，公司還欠供應商錢。被欠錢的一方是 creditor。
usage: debtor is a person or firm that owes money. The bank listed three debtors who were late with payments.
debtor 是欠錢的人或公司。
investor puts money into a company to earn a return. Investors bought shares in the new firm.
investor 是投資公司以求回報的人。
auditor checks a company's accounts. The auditors will review our records in April.
auditor 是查核公司帳目的人。

gloss.ex: Please send the invoice by email.
Please pay the invoice in full.
The finance director approved the new budget.

why: Each breakdown was traced to a worn belt that should have been replaced months earlier. The breakdowns did happen, but they could have been avoided: preventable.
每次故障都 was traced to a worn belt that should have been replaced months earlier。故障確實發生了，但本來可以避免：preventable。
usage: preventive describes action taken to stop problems: preventive maintenance. The plant schedules preventive checks every month.
preventive 形容用來預防問題的做法：preventive maintenance。
prevented is the past of prevent: stopped before it happened. Early checks prevented a longer shutdown.
prevented 是 prevent 的過去式：在事情發生前就阻止。
preventing needs an object after it: preventing accidents. Preventing delays is the supervisor's main job.
preventing 後面要接受詞：preventing accidents。

gloss.ex: A breakdown stopped the line for an hour.
The worn tires need to be replaced.
The fault was traced to a loose cable.

why: Staff usually book the one in the south building instead, so the old north elevator has never been reliable: dependable.
員工 usually book the one in the south building instead，表示北棟舊貨梯一直不可靠：dependable。
usage: dependent on someone or something: relying on it. The small shop is dependent on one supplier.
dependent on 人或物：依賴它。
depending on something means it varies with that thing. Prices change, depending on the season.
depending on 某事：隨該事而不同，即「視……而定」。
depend on someone: rely on them. We depended on the night shift to finish the order.
depend on 人：倚靠他們。

gloss.ex: Use the freight elevator for boxes.
The crew moved the heavy equipment by truck.
